Gary Lyndon Dye

Libertarian candidate for US Senator, Oregon · Challenger

Engineer and technical consultant (former gas measurement engineer at NW Natural)

Gary Lyndon Dye is a Portland-born chemical engineer, physicist and author running for U.S. Senate as the Libertarian nominee in Oregon's November 3, 2026 general election. He was the Libertarian nominee for this Senate seat in 2020 and received about 1.8% of the vote. He has also run for the U.S. House (Oregon District 3), the Oregon House and Metro Council President.

Where Dye stands

Taxes / IRS
Proposes abolishing the IRS and replacing most federal taxes with a single-rate Universal Transaction Tax on every exchange of money. He would then raise the rate and cut government until the deficit and debt are paid off.
Universal basic income / welfare
Proposes paying every citizen a Universal Basic Income and eliminating the welfare bureaucracy, alongside cuts to entitlement programs.
National debt / federal spending
Says both parties have spent heavily and warns the economy will crash if the growth of the national debt is not reversed. Supports balancing the budget by cutting government.
Property tax
Calls the property tax a regressive wealth tax and supports ending it.
Social Security / retirement
Proposes converting the Social Security, Medicare and federal employee trust funds into a sovereign wealth fund and moving government pensions to 401(k)s. Opposes pensions for politicians.
Foreign policy / military
Supports bringing U.S. troops home, defending North America under a renewed Monroe Doctrine, and lending military support only when allies are attacked. Supports suspending all foreign aid.
United Nations / diplomacy
Proposes withdrawing from the UN until every member is a democracy and cutting ties with dictatorships.
Immigration / citizenship
Proposes treating U.S. citizenship as an individual property right that citizens could sell. Government, corporations or charities could buy or subsidize citizenships for newcomers.
Role of government
Says most things government manages are not legitimate government functions. Pledges to work to reduce or eliminate them rather than expand them.

Background

  • Libertarian nominee, U.S. Senate, Oregon, 2026
  • Libertarian nominee, U.S. Senate, Oregon, 2020 (about 1.8%, 42,747 votes)
  • Candidate, U.S. House, Oregon District 3, 2018 and 2024
  • Candidate, Metro Council President, 2022
  • Candidate, Oregon House of Representatives, 2016 (4.7%)
  • Technical consultant, 2015–present
  • Gas measurement engineer, NW Natural, 2000–2012
  • Chief process engineer, Saudi Aramco, 1996–1997
  • B.S. Chemical Engineering, Oregon State University (1981); MBA, Pepperdine University (1989); B.S. Physics/Applied Mathematics, UC Irvine (1991)
